clues: A megacity crowds both banks of a great river flowing north through the desert, just above where the river fans into a wide green delta.
Some years see no rain at all — yet each spring a hot dust wind roars off the desert, pushing past forty degrees and choking the streets.
A conquering army founded it in 641 beside an old river fortress; it grew rich on the trade road between two seas and raised a thousand minarets.
Its museum once held a boy king's solid-gold funeral mask, found untouched in a small tomb cut into the southern desert cliffs.
The Pyramids of Giza — the last surviving wonder of the ancient world — stand on the desert plateau at the city's edge.
